summary: 79-year-old frail woman with a full-thickness rectal prolapse that has been out and irreducible for 6 hours, oedematous with a dusky segment. Emergency: attempt reduction (sedation, sugar/osmotic), emergency perineal rectosigmoidectomy (Altemeier) if non-viable or irreducible.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Bowel coming out of the back passage and will not go back
inputs.hpi: Known rectal prolapse for 2 years, usually reduces after bowel motions. Since this morning (6 h) it has stayed out and she cannot push it back; very painful, some bleeding. Constipated. Lives in a care home; walks with a frame. Heart failure.

exam.other: 10 cm full-thickness rectal prolapse (concentric folds), oedematous, with a dusky, dark segment anteriorly; not reducible with gentle pressure.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Incarcerated full-thickness rectal prolapse, possible strangulation
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Incarcerated full-thickness rectal prolapse with a dusky segment in a frail 79-year-old. Emergency reduction attempt; perineal rectosigmoidectomy if non-viable or irreducible.

emergencyLevel.note: Incarcerated prolapse with a dusky segment: strangulation must be assumed; same-day surgical care.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — treatment of rectal prolapse
guideline.section: Incarcerated or strangulated prolapse: reduction if viable; perineal rectosigmoidectomy for non-viable bowel; perineal procedures favoured in frail patients
guideline.citation: Bordeianou L, Paquette I, Johnson E, et al. Clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of rectal prolapse. Dis Colon Rectum. 2017;60:1121–1131.

rationale: Base prolapse case, chosen as the dangerous variant (incarceration/strangulation). The web presentation chip "rectal prolapse" is a symptom chip; the template is generic.
